useFor: A condition of the page that stays true while it is open, such as read-only access, a service that is slow or a form that was not saved, said in place above what it is about.

combineWith.how: Straight on .page between the sections it is about, spaced by the page's own rhythm with no margin of its own.
Above the card whose controls it explains, as read-only mode does, so the reason is read before the disabled buttons.
A validation summary goes at the top of the form and links to each field, and every field keeps its own .form-error.
The receipt for the same event, once nothing is left for the reader to do.

notFor.text: A receipt for something the reader just did
A notice about the whole app, such as an outage or a maintenance window
A caveat about one card's own data
A permanent aside inside prose
A question that must be answered before anything else happens

useFor: A receipt for something the reader just did, which goes on its own and would change nothing if it were missed.

combineWith.how: Whatever stays true, or still needs the reader, goes in an alert in the page; the toast only reports that something happened.
A notification that arrives is added to the inbox and may also be presented as a toast the app writes, never only as one.
A .spinner in the icon's place for a toast that stands for work still running, replaced in place by its outcome.

notFor.text: An error the reader must fix, or anything they need later
Something to come back to later
A question that must be answered before going on
A message about one field
An action that ended on another page, after a redirect

useFor: What happened while the reader was elsewhere, kept behind a bell with an unread count until they have seen it.

combineWith.how: The bell is a .topbar-btn at the header's end, its unread count in the button's name.
The panel is a .popover the bell opens with popovertarget, so the platform places it, closes it and returns the focus.
All, Unread and Archived as .tabs with .inbox-tabs, under the panel's head.
An item's further actions, such as mark as read, snooze and archive, behind one button at its end.
Who it is from at the start of each item; an item from the system is an icon in an avatar.
A tab with nothing in it shows an empty state in the list's place, in words for that tab.
Announces an item as it arrives, beside adding it to the list.

notFor.text: A receipt for what the reader just did
Something that must be answered before anything else
The history of one record, told as events

useFor: Saying that work is under way: a bar or a ring with its figure where the share done is known, a spinner where it is not, and aria-busy on whatever is busy.

combineWith.how: An action in flight is aria-busy on its own button, which keeps its width, its focus and its name.
Running work is a list with one row per job, the bar under its title and the figure, a spinner or a badge at its end.
Finished work trades its bar for a badge that says the outcome in words.
Each file being uploaded carries its own bar with the figure beside it.
A wait with no figure but a known shape shows the shape instead of a spinner.

notFor.text: A value against a limit with its thresholds marked
A wait whose content has a known shape
A panel with nothing to show yet
The steps of a task the reader moves through

useFor: The first load of content whose shape is known: placeholders the size of the rows, fields and figures to come, so nothing moves when they arrive.

combineWith.how: A whole list page loading: the real toolbar and table headings, skeleton rows under them, and the count saying what is loading.
Inside the real card and its head, so the card holds its place while its body loads.
The real .list rows with placeholders where the title, the line under it and the badge go.
Stat tiles with the value's box held at the figure's height, since the figure is what the reader waits for.
A skeleton block in the chart's place until the table it draws arrives.
A refresh of content already shown keeps the content and marks it aria-busy instead.

notFor.text: A refresh of content already on screen
A wait with a known percentage
A view that has loaded and holds nothing

useFor: A view with nothing to show, or nothing yet: saying which kind of empty it is, or that it failed, and giving the one action that resolves it.

combineWith.how: The drawing above the title names the state at a glance; a state icon takes its place where the missing thing has a glyph.
Inside the card of the panel it stands for, in the content's place, with the card's head still above it.
In a table, in one full-width row under the real headings.
In a list, in the place of its rows.
Each inbox tab with nothing in it says so in words for that tab.
At page scale, .empty-state--page is the body of not found, access denied and the error page.

notFor.text: A wait for content with a known shape
A wait with a percentage
A condition of a page that still shows its content
A whole page that is an error or a refusal

useFor: The drawing that names a view's state before its sentence is read: nothing yet, filtered out, failed, offline, waiting, all done.

combineWith.how: Above the empty state's title and aria-hidden, since the title says the same in words.
The small size in a table row with nothing in it.
The small size in a list's place when the list is empty.
The large size on a page that is nothing but the state.

notFor.text: A missing thing that has a glyph of its own, such as invoices or members
A picture that is part of the content

useFor: What a view shows while something is still happening: the state of a connection, output being written, how long ago or how long left, and work the reader can watch and cancel.

combineWith.how: The connection to the server is the status bar's; a health badge reports a service or a stream inside the page.
A degraded page says once, in a page banner, what is down and what still works.
A figure that could not be read is .stat--unavailable with a .stale saying how old the last good one is.
Work in progress is a .list-row with its bar in the subtext and its cancel button in .list-meta.
A countdown inside the warning dialog that offers to keep the reader signed in.
The same pane as an application log, with columns, levels and rows that expand.

notFor.text: A panel with nothing to show yet
The first load of content with a known shape
The connection to the server itself
A share done with no output to show

useFor: An app's own log or a developer's output read in place: lines in columns by level, a live tail, rows that expand and act, a terminal, a stack trace and test results.

combineWith.how: Above the pane: the search and the level chips leading, the wrapping setting and the refresh trailing.
The level filter as pressed chips, each with the number of lines it holds.
Wrap or one line, as a small segmented setting in the toolbar.
A line's further actions behind one button in its .output-actions strip, after the copy button.
The time range, opened from a .form-trigger at the start of the toolbar.
A test run's passed, failed and skipped as one bar in parts above the suites, its legend in words.
Environment variables as key/value rows in a card, with a copy and a reveal button each.
Skeleton lines in the pane for the first load.

notFor.text: Records compared down columns and sorted
The history of one record, told as events
Code shown for the reader to copy
